facts.target_definition: 1 = bad risk (credit contract not complied with), 0 = good risk

narrative.purpose: Flag existing borrowers at elevated risk of default for early outreach. Business use: Prioritising collections contact lists.
narrative.methodology: Single classification tree (CART) that splits applicants into a small number of leaves; the PD is the (re-weighted) default share in the leaf.
assumptions: Risk is constant within each leaf.
The tree structure found on the development sample is stable.
limitations: Produces a handful of distinct scores, so ranking within a leaf is impossible.
Class weighting ('balanced') inflates PDs: scores are rankings, not calibrated probabilities.
Developed on 1,000 historical German loans from 1973-1975: a small, old, non-UK sample used here as a stand-in for bank data.
risks: Uses age (protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010) as a direct input. Requires a documented justification and fairness testing before use in customer decisions.
Documentation last reviewed 2021-07 (5.4 years ago): out of date.
Coarse scores may produce cliff-edge decisions for similar customers.
